"Studying after school: I spend an average of 2-5 hours studying most days after school. Making checklist of shit to do helps keep track of what you should prioritise (If you're doing low res consistently, brain rot is crazy lmao, you're going to NEED a checklist). Don't be lazy. HTTPURL"

"Study Method Cont: If I'm trying to cram, I will go over to some youtube channels and play a summary video full speed. One of the most important factors is to always do exam questions, correct them yourself and do it again. It's a good way to answer accurately using keywords HTTPURL"

"Study Methods: My method is to firstly look over class notes, then read through the textbook if I don't understand. I will try active recall and summarise topics with post-it notes then fill in the gaps. I may try practice questions and make flashcards following the spec after. HTTPURL"

"Focus: I sometimes buy glucose and caffeine shots for a pretty good price, they are usually chewable and sweet. If I really need it, I will also buy focus vitamins that better my performance. Apps/Websites like forest and hours can keep you in check and boost productivity. HTTPURL"

"Health: Try to keep on top of your vitamins, take supplements if you need to and DRINK WATER. If you are a period-haver, stock up on iron in advance. If you have a fitness watch, keep track of your heart rate and sleep quality if you can. Up your intake, if needed, exercise more. HTTPURL"

"Diet: I tend to do high res during school and med-low res during the term holidays. Focus on high protein and low fats. Spinach, almond milk and eggs are incredibly useful :) It's ideal that I fast between 18-22 hours a day. Shorter consistent fasts are way better than long ones. HTTPURL"

"Studying during school: I get free study periods around 4-5 hours a week and I tend to use it to complete as much homework in advance as possible. This also gives me a chance to play Subliminals through my earphones while studying and fidget to burn more calories. HTTPURL"
